I am old now, sixty years, and I have farmed beans on this land for many seasons. The fertilizer is too costly for me, and beans do not need it like maize — they feed themselves from the soil. I will use the seeds I saved from last harvest, like my mother taught me, and put some manure from the goats on the land before planting. My sons and grandchildren will help me weed, and if the work is too much I will call one or two people from the village to help for a few days.
